key_insight: A multi-stage explainability pipeline can turn a transformer’s speech-based cognitive impairment prediction into a clinician-friendly explanation grounded in linguistic features and SHAP attributions.
clinical_relevance: This could make speech screening for cognitive impairment more interpretable and easier to integrate into clinical workflows without relying on invasive biomarker tests.
method: Built on the SpeechCARE-Adaptive Gating Network multimodal screening model.
Uses SHAP to identify influential speech tokens and maps them to four cognitive-linguistic dimensions.
Adds a four-stage LLM reasoning pipeline with LLaMA-3.1-70B-Instruct to generate clinically grounded narratives.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on 70 stratified English samples, with physician assessments showing strong alignment to cognitive profiles and a System Usability Scale score of 82/100.
watch_item: The approach was tested on a limited English sample set, so broader validation across languages, sites, and patient populations is still needed.
paper_title: From Black-Box to Clinical Insight: A Multi-Stage Explainable Framework for Speech-Based Cognitive Impairment Detection
